details.label: Discussion
details.text: Surface analysis shows substantial moisture across eastern CO and into southeast WY, with upper 50s to lower 60s F dewpoints. Daytime heating continues, with weak easterly surface winds maintaining the moist air mass. Lapse rates are not particularly steep today, with warm temperatures aloft, and lack of boundary layer mixing. However, MLCAPE is increasing to around 2000 J/kg, and, 20 to 30 kt mid to high level winds are resulting in effective deep layer shear of 30 kt. As such, mixed storm modes are expected. A strong cell has already developed over western Douglas County as of 20Z, possibly producing hail. Additional activity will likely fill in across the entire region through early evening, and some cells may produce hail over 1.00" diameter. Some of the downdrafts may produce strong to perhaps severe gusts, but an organized wind threat is not anticipated

details.label: Summary
details.text: Lop-topped thunderstorms may bring an isolated risk for damaging wind gusts (and perhaps an instance of marginally severe hail) to portions of New York and southern New England this afternoon

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Regional radar imagery depicts a cluster of ongoing thunderstorms that have recently progressed from southern Ontario into Upstate New York immediately ahead of a mid-level shortwave trough evident in visible satellite imagery. Cold mid-level temperatures associated with this shortwave and steep low-level lapse rates have allowed for the development of weak buoyancy (on the order of a few hundred J/kg MLCAPE), which is sufficient for a few relatively low-topped thunderstorms. Strong northwesterly, mid-to-upper level flow (sampled by the TYX VWP) is supporting modest effective shear (25-35+ kts) and some updraft organization. While it remains unclear how long ongoing convection will be maintained owing to limited available buoyancy, forcing associated with the mid-level shortwave may allow for the persistence of ongoing convection southeastward toward southern New England and/or additional downstream development through the afternoon. Should this occur, isolated damaging wind gusts (and perhaps an instance of marginally severe hail in the near-term) are possible. Watch issuance is not anticipated as the limited thermodynamic environment is expected to largely temper convective intensity

details.label: Summary
details.text: A locally greater risk for damaging wind gusts may develop across across portions of the NC/VA Piedmont downstream of developing thunderstorms

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest surface analysis depicts a quasi-stationary/weak cold frontal boundary extending roughly west-to-east from southern DelMarVa into central Virginia and the central Appalachians. South of this boundary, continued insolation and dewpoints in the low 70s F should support 1500-2500+ J/kg MLCAPE by peak heating this afternoon, sufficient for a few stronger updrafts. Effective shear remains generally weak roughly south of the NC/VA border (less than 20 kts), which will favor an outflow-dominant/pulse-severe type storm mode. Steepening low-level lapse rates and high PW (2+ inches per the 12 UTC GSO observed sounding) will support an isolated risk for wet microbursts and damaging wind gusts. Farther north, latest objective analysis suggests that effective shear is locally enhanced along the aforementioned surface boundary (20-30+ kts) across central/southern Virginia. This could allow for a locally greater risk for damaging wind gusts to materialize should a loosely organized cluster evolve east-southeastward out of West Virginia (where a recent report of thunderstorm wind damage is noted). Regardless, the overall severe risk is expected to remain relatively isolated and limited in magnitude. Thus, watch issuance appears unlikely at this time
